variant.description: hooks module under vbpm.variants that owns the model; base is tutorial 7 (encoder-deployed, no conditional prior). A new recipe is a new module plus a new config, never a flag in run.py.

emission.description: p(y | phi) shape. cosine is the tutorial's own a + b cos(phi); triangle is the symmetric tent, non-zero across the whole bar; laplace replaces a rectangular window's far edge with an exponential tail, keeping band's asymmetry while restoring a gradient at every phase, and its decay length is a continuous parameter rather than an integer width; alaplace gives that decay a second, independent scale running backward from the onset, which removes laplace's late bias -- the tent and the one-sided band are the two corners of this family -- and lets the data set the asymmetry; bump is the von Mises-shaped narrow peak whose width is emission_bump_kappa.

emission_layers.description: transformer emission only: number of attention layers. Ignored by the closed-form emissions.

emission_positional.description: transformer emission only: add positional encoding, letting the emission read FRAME INDEX as well as phase.

emission_bump_kappa.description: bump emission only: concentration of the peak. The bump is exp(kappa (cos phi - 1)), so its half-width is about sqrt(2/kappa) radians of bar phase.

target_tol_frames.description: half-width in frames of the framewise target y. 0 is the tutorial's own b (eq 55): one frame per downbeat, at which point the two emission_recon terms are identical by construction. Widening it smears one downbeat over 2n+1 frames, which no longer is b.

chain_bins.description: schain only: phase cells. Bin width is one bar / chain_bins, so it bounds placement resolution; 96 is about 21 ms on a 2 s bar.

chain_rate_grid.description: schain only: enumerated rate candidates, log-spaced. Each runs its own chain, so cost is linear in this.

chain_posterior.description: schain only: chain is the structured posterior; frames is the factorised control that switches the coupling off while keeping everything else identical.

epochs.description: training epochs; one fresh window per song per epoch.

batch_size.description: windows per step, shared by training and evaluation.

lr.description: Adam learning rate for the single base parameter group.

clip.description: gradient-norm clip over the params the variant's optimizer hook hands back.

pos_weight.description: positive-class weight in the Bernoulli reconstruction. Anything but 1 is a surrogate, not an ELBO.

beta_end.description: KL weight after warmup; the reported elbo is always beta = 1.

beta_warmup.description: epochs to ramp beta linearly from beta_start to beta_end; 0 disables annealing.

emission_sharpness.description: scheduled floor on the emission amplitude b (closed-form emissions only); 0 leaves b free.

sharpness_warmup.description: epochs over which the emission_sharpness floor ramps in.

excerpt_seconds.description: window length. Below ~45 s the ELBO cannot separate tracking the truth from coasting on a constant period (crop-horizon root cause).

prior_phase_kappa.description: concentration of the physical prior's increment law: the DRIFT TAX. Real tempo wobble is heavy-tailed, so lowering this cuts the KL price of expressing drift.

tempo_prior_mu.description: mean of p(log dotphi_1), the ONLY term pricing tempo LEVEL (the walk prices changes, not the level, so a random walk is indifferent to which octave it sits in). Refit on train folds: 1665 songs, mean log bar rate -2.6827 = 1.84 s per bar. The shipped -2.5028 (1.53 s) put the octave flip point at 2.17 s, so songs slower than that were pushed to 2x.

tempo_prior_sigma.description: sd of p(log dotphi_1), refit on the same train folds (shipped 0.5005). Narrower makes the level prior more opinionated, which moves the octave flip point out to 2.60 s.

walk_sigma.description: per-frame sd of the tempo walk: how much log tempo may change between adjacent frames. One number for every song, which the corpus says it cannot be -- per-song variability spans 20x (hjdb 0.005 to asap 0.077 per bar) and is a stable property of a performance (split-half r 0.81). Held-out fit favours a per-song scale by +2.2 nats/step over any global value, and heavy tails by only +0.9.

phase_init.description: where phi_1 comes from. anchor takes the closed-form circular mean of the encoder's evidence channel folded under the mean ramp -- the read-out that carried 82% of the anchor jump. uniform draws it at random, which leaves nothing anchoring placement and was committed at 89cb1f7 as an explicit null.

frontend.description: module under vbpm.data.frontends supplying features + activations. The frontend is part of the model, not preprocessing (see vbpm-checkpoint-artifact).

frontend_checkpoint.description: checkpoint the frontend loads; ONE serves train/val/test alike. final0 is Beat This's (gtzan held out of every checkpoint); beat_transformer wants e.g. fold_0.

frontend_lr_scale.description: multiplier on lr for the frontend's own parameters. 0 = frozen (the frontend runs under no_grad and only the VAE trains); > 0 thaws it and adds it as a second optimizer group at lr * this. RECONSTRUCTED 2026-08-11 after an accidental git checkout discarded the uncommitted original -- the semantics come from run.py's usage, the wording is not the author's.

clip_per_group.description: clip each parameter tensor against cfg.clip separately instead of one pooled norm (which one tensor dominated, throttling all others). Changes the log's |g|: pooled norm when false, largest single-tensor norm when true.

lambda_distill.description: psi only: weight on KL(q || p_psi), the term that buys transfer to the deployed prior. It used to enter hardcoded at 1.0 while lambda_prior weighted only prior_anchor -- measured at init, distill was 355 nats/frame against recon 0.11 and prior_anchor 2.5, so ~99% of the objective was untunable and every past lambda_prior sweep moved the wrong term.

lambda_tempo.description: psi only: weight on an explicit log-dotphi distillation, mean-squared (log dotphi_p - log dotphi_q). 0 reproduces the old behaviour. Motivation: in a transfer experiment against a known teacher on input where the tempo is trivially readable, the ANCHOR converged every run (0.000-0.015 of a bar) while the RATE was a lottery (0.08%-60.9%, median ~25%) at every kappa from 0.1 to 383 -- through a phase density a tempo error only arrives as accumulated phase.

phi0_posterior.description: q(phi_0) comes from its own boundary head instead of the anchor's point mass. The note's eq (7): the first latent is a von Mises like every other frame, so the initial KL is finite and closed form and the chain has something for later evidence to reweight.

posterior_reads_b.description: q reads the labels as well as the audio, and a second audio-only network becomes the conditional prior p_eta(z | x). The note's asymmetry: x is in every factor, b only in the posterior. Deployment then reads the prior, since b is absent at inference.

emission_frozen.description: hold the emission's offset, gain and decay scales fixed at their initial values; the rest of the model still trains.

bar_walk_sigma.description: sd of the Gaussian walk on log-rate BETWEEN BARS, the only place the rate may move. Per-frame walk laws are all refuted (audit 2026-08-19); a bar-gated increment is the law the bar-gated chain already assumed, priced continuously instead of through a 36-atom grid.

delta_rel.description: cap on the per-frame phase correction as a fraction of the current rate; the cap enters q and its KL alike, so it restricts the family without breaking the bound.

kappa_q_min.description: floor on the posterior concentration of a phase step, so a diffuse step stays numerically finite.

emission_nested.description: factorise the class emission as p(beat | phi, m) * p(downbeat | beat, phi) with a Bernoulli per factor, instead of a softmax over {N, B, D}. A downbeat is then a beat rather than its exclusive alternative, so the beat channel is rewarded at phase 0 instead of losing there to the downbeat class.

emission_floor.description: probability that a downbeat annotation is drawn from a phase-independent background rather than from the emission's shape, which bounds what a misplaced downbeat can cost; 0 is the plain Bernoulli emission.

tempo_per_bar.description: the rate may change at a wrapping phase transition, paying the wrapped-Cauchy cost on log-rate; false makes the switch the identity, so one rate carries the whole window -- the rigid control.

meters.description: beats-per-bar values the chain enumerates; at least one is required. Meter joins rate in the state and may change only at a wrapping phase transition.

meter_prior.description: p(m): corpus is the song-weighted share measured over 4,900 songs in sixteen corpora -- 0.831 on m=4, 0.012 on m=8. uniform is available as an ablation, and charges nothing for a meter the corpus almost never contains.
